extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities, applicants, counsel, and interested persons responding to Federal Register notices and administrative agency proceedings (e.g., FERC/Natural Gas Commission, SEC, ICC, SBA)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural requirements and substantive standards governing filings, protests, hearing requests, interventions, exemptions, and agency orders as published in Federal Register notices from various agencies (Natural Gas Commission/FERC, SEC, ICC, SBA). Useful for parties preparing or responding to administrative applications and notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness rule for competitive natural gas applications (Natural Gas Act §157.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a competitive application 'is filed less than 15 days prior to the commencement of a hearing' 'the Commission will not schedule the new application for hearing until it has rendered its final decision on such pending application, except when, it finds that the public interest requires otherwise.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text explains the Commission's default to defer scheduling of late-filed competitive applications unless the public interest requires otherwise; examples and factual analysis (e.g., CP68-70 public notice timing) are used to determine whether a purportedly 'late' filing is untimely within the meaning of the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation and reopening — public interest / equity balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions to consolidate and reopen dockets weigh potential delay against the opportunity to consider the optimum method of providing service and to afford full equity among affected parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice explains that although consolidation/reopening may delay service to some customers, this potential detriment can be outweighed by the public interest in considering all proposals together, possible cost savings (example: reduction by 14 cents per Mcf), and avoiding disadvantaging parties who would otherwise be heard only after certificates are issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting petitions to intervene
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to intervene by parties having an interest in the proceedings (e.g., Juarez Gas, Juarez Transportation, Del Norte, Southern Union) may be filed and will be considered and, where appropriate, granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission granted motions to consolidate and reopen and granted petitions to intervene by the listed parties in the consolidated dockets; intervention is treated as part of procedural disposition when consolidation/reopening is ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditioning certificates to secure required supply or rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may condition any certificates it issues to require an appropriate portion of gas involved in related dockets be sold to a party (e.g., require El Paso to sell an appropriate portion of gas to Juarez Transportation) if such conditions serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice states the Commission can impose such conditions but does not pass on the merits here; affected parties (e.g., El Paso) will have full opportunity in reopened hearings to submit evidence regarding such conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of intermediate decision procedure — premature petition standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to waive the intermediate decision procedure may be denied as premature when consolidation and reopening make such a waiver inappropriate at the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Del Norte's petition to waive the intermediate decision was denied in part as premature given the Commission's decision to consolidate and reopen the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC summary suspension standard (section 15(c)(5) of Exchange Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary suspension of trading in securities may be ordered 'in the public interest and for the protection of investors' pursuant to section 15(c)(5) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied in the Order Suspending Trading for Interamerican Industries, Ltd.; the order specifies effective dates for the summary suspension and is framed as an action required when the Commission finds such suspension necessary for investor protection/public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust Indenture Act §310(b) — conflicting interest rule and trustee obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a trustee under an indenture 'has or shall acquire any conflicting interest' it must within 90 days after ascertaining it has such a conflicting interest 'either eliminate such conflicting interest or resign.' A trustee is deemed to have a conflicting interest if it is trustee under another indenture under which other securities of the same issuer are outstanding, with certain exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clause (ii) of subsection (1) permits exclusion of another indenture if the issuer sustains its burden on application to the Commission, after opportunity for hearing, that trusteeship under both indentures is not so likely to involve a material conflict of interest as to require disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden and process for exclusion under §310(b)(1)(ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: To exclude an indenture from the conflicting-interest rule under clause (ii), the issuer must 'sustain the burden of proving, on application to the Commission and after opportunity for hearing thereon, that trusteeship under the indentures is not so likely to involve a material conflict of interest' as to require disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications under this provision are filed with the Commission, may be published as notices, and interested persons may request hearings; the notices provide factual examples (e.g., Ralston Purina and Southern Union) of how issuers characterize parity, security terms, and subsidiary guarantees to show lack of material conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request a hearing on SEC applications and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested person may, not later than the specified date in the notice, request in writing that a hearing be held, stating the nature of his interest, the reasons for such request, and the issues of fact or law raised by the application which he desires to controvert; or may request notification if the Commission orders a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices give specific deadlines (e.g., January 29, 1968; January 25, 1968; January 24, 1968) and the address (Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, Washington, D.C.). The Commission may issue an order granting the application on the basis of the information on file unless a hearing is ordered. Parties sometimes waive notice and hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption under Investment Company Act §6(c) — public interest/investor protection standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may exempt any person, security, or transaction from provisions of the Act if 'such exemption is necessary or appropriate in the public interest and consistent with the protection of investors and the purposes fairly intended by the policy and provisions of the Act.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for exemptions (e.g., underwriters' participation in underwriting of Fund shares) must include representations (e.g., absence of inside or special information) and are published for comment with deadlines for requests for hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest filing requirements for ICC motor carrier temporary authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests to the granting of a temporary motor carrier application 'must be filed with the field office named in the Federal Register publication, within 15 calendar days after the date of notice of the filing of the application is published in the Federal Register.' One copy must be served on the applicant and service must be certified. Protests must be specific as to the service the protestant can and will offer and must consist of a signed original and six copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice describes where to send protests (named District Supervisors at specified addresses), requires certification of service, and explains that a copy of the application can be examined at the Office of the Secretary and the relevant field office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in motor carrier temporary authority notices/applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A temporary authority notice/application must identify the applicant, applicant's representative, the authority sought (e.g., common/contract carrier, route type), the commodity to be transported (including any bulk/tank specifications), origin and destination points, duration of the requested authority, and supporting shipper(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published notices provide concrete examples (e.g., Consolidated Freightways seeking to transport benzoic acid in bulk from Kalama, Wash., to Niagara Falls, N.Y.; American Courier Corporation describing commercial papers between specified counties) that illustrate the expected level of specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republication/correction practice for Federal Register notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an earlier publication contained errors (e.g., wrong shipper location or misworded commodity description), the notice may be republished as corrected in a later Federal Register issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the text show reasons for republication (correct location of shipper, correction of commodity description wording) and indicate that republication is used to ensure accurate public notice for protest and comment deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBA disaster declaration criteria and loan application window
rubrics_metrics.description: A disaster loan area is declared where investigations and reports show that conditions 'constitute a catastrophe within the purview of the Small Business Act'; following such a determination, applications for disaster loans under section 7(b)(1) may be received from persons/firms whose property in the affected county and adjacent areas suffered damage, and a cutoff date for acceptance of applications is specified (e.g., applications will not be accepted subsequent to June 30, 1968).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice identifies the affected county (Washington County, Mo.), the disaster date (tornado occurring on December 20, 1967), the local SBA office for submission, and the statutory basis for receiving and processing disaster loan applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and filing proofs for requests and protests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for hearings, protests, and similar filings that must be served on applicants require proof of service (affidavit or attorney certificate) to be filed contemporaneously and, in some contexts, personal or mailed (airmail if over 500 miles) service is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices instruct that a copy of any hearing request must be served personally or by mail on applicants and proof of such service must be filed contemporaneously; the Investment Company Act notice gives explicit instruction on service to applicants and proof of service requirements.
